claim: Vera's runtime spends the CHEAPEST faculty that is actually sufficient for a task, and stops. For every task the LERF Runtime Router walks an escalating ladder — a deterministic rule (~free) -> a LIRF memory lookup -> a retrieved LERF skill (~hundreds of tokens) -> a small local render of that skill -> a GROUNDED verifier that checks the render against the skill's contract -> and ONLY on verifier failure (or when nothing local has standing and a cloud brain is available) does it escalate to a larger/cloud model ($$ + data egress). It returns the FIRST rung that suffices with a readable {route, why, fallback}; the decision is deterministic (same task -> identical Route). The verifier is a real gate, never a rubber stamp: a render that fabricates a figure or goes off-contract is WITHHELD (never served) when no cloud is available. This router is wired into the live turn: anima/server._lerf_eligible calls route_task to decide whether a turn is a LERF-skill task before the model is ever consulted, and again (rung 5) to adjudicate the small-model render and withhold a contract-violating one.
owner: anima/lerf_router.py (route_task = the six-rung cheapest-sufficient ladder returning a frozen Route{route,why,fallback,rung,cost_tier,considered,skill_id,score,escalated,grounded}; the COST table enforcing free<lookup<tokens<local<cloud; SKILL_MATCH_FLOOR; the pure rung probes _rule_hit/_lirf_hit/_skill_hit/_cloud_available; explain_route prose; --selftest), anima/lerf.py (retrieve_skills/_score/verify_rendered_output — the substrate the router plans over), anima/server.py (_lerf_eligible gates the turn on route_task's rung-3 decision; _lerf_task_first re-enters route_task with rendered= to adjudicate rung 5 and WITHHOLD a failed render; _turn calls _lerf_eligible at the top of every reply)

known_gaps: The router is a PURE deterministic planner: it never itself calls a model. Rungs 4-6 (small-local render, cloud escalation) are EXECUTED by anima/server._lerf_task_first, which drives the small local model and re-enters route_task for the rung-5 verdict; the small-model GENERATION and the cloud call are the only legs that need a live model, so they are out of scope for this offline cert. What this cert proves is the routing DECISION + the grounded WITHHOLD, both deterministic, and that they are wired into the live server turn (server._lerf_eligible, exercised here on the real function).

The rung-2 LIRF and rung-1 deterministic-rule legs are exercised through the router's own probes (with no fact on the synthetic ledger, a fact-question correctly falls through rather than confabulating); a fully-populated ledger answer is proven by the known_fact_memory feature, not re-proven here.
